title: General Contractor Invoice Template
subtitle: An invoice pre-filled for GC billing — materials, subcontractors, crew labor, permits, equipment and cleanup. Download as Excel (auto-calculating), Word, or PDF.
taxHint: Look up your state's sales tax rate
paymentTerms: Net 14 — payment due within 14 days of invoice date. Late fee of 1.5% per month applies after the due date.
notes: Thank you for your business. This invoice covers work completed to date; change orders are billed separately.
features: Auto-calculating tax formulas in Excel (just enter your state rate)
Pre-filled GC line items: materials, subcontractors, crew labor, permits, equipment, cleanup
License # field — most states require a contractor license on client-facing invoices
Change-order note keeps scope changes billable

faqs.q: What should I include on a general contractor invoice?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name and license number, the client and job-site address, dated line items for materials, subcontractors, labor, permits, equipment and cleanup, tax, and a total due. Most states require a contractor license number on client-facing documents.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate tax automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, tax and total update automatically. Leave the tax rate blank if you are not required to charge sales tax.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your contractor board and a CPA or attorney before use.
